gap: No result ChatGPT got says that OUPES's add-on hardware only fits the Mega line. OUPES's own US store lists the B2 extra battery as "Compatible with the Mega 1/2/3 & Titan 3 Power Station" and the 800W alternator charger as "Made for Mega & Guardian Series. Not for Exodus Series or other Brands". So the Exodus 1200 that most of the results review can never take a second battery or alternator charging, and neither compatibility list names the $599 Mega 1 Lite.
standout_why: I compared six of the nine results. shopsavvy.com (Exodus 1200 TLDR), activegearreview.com (Exodus 1200), nerdtechy.com (1100W) and maketecheasier.com (1100W) never mention expansion batteries or an alternator charger. oupes.com/pages/off-grid-power-station sells a "Mega 1 + B2 Extra Battery" bundle and lists the 800W alternator charger, but it never says which stations each one works with or that the Exodus line is excluded. So the maker's page implies part of it but never says it outright. I couldn't open the oupes.com Mega product page (result 6) or the collection page (result 3) because the site returned HTTP 429. I didn't open the rv-pro.com news item (result 7).
decides: If the shopper may want more runtime later or charging from a vehicle while driving, the pick is the Mega 1 ($699 on oupes.com today). It is "Expandable Up to 5.12kWh with B2*2" and works with the alternator charger. Skip the Exodus 1200 ($549 on oupes.com, listed as sold out) and Exodus 700 ($399). They are fixed-capacity units, and OUPES excludes the Exodus series from its alternator charger by name. The Mega 1 Lite ($599) costs $100 less than the Mega 1, but neither its own listing nor the B2's compatibility list says it can expand. Treat it as fixed-capacity unless OUPES confirms otherwise. If 1 kWh is enough for good, the Exodus 1200's fixed design doesn't matter, but its "1,500W Boost Mode" is a voltage-lowering mode, not true 1,500 W output (see TheSolarLab finding).

findings.value: 992 Wh; 1,200 W rated ("1,500W Boost Mode"); "Instant UPS Backup < 20ms"; 840 W max input (AC + solar); 23.15 lb; $549 (compare-at $799), listed as "(Sold Out)"
findings.source_title: (Sold Out) OUPES Exodus 1200 Portable Power Station | 1200W 992Wh
findings.note: Read from oupes.com store product data with storecheck.py. The listing names no expansion battery. shopsavvy.com and activegearreview.com cite a 3,600 W surge, but the maker's listing gives only the 1,200 W rating and 1,500 W boost.

findings.label: What boost mode actually does (TheSolarLab test)
findings.value: In a 1,500 W heat-gun test the unit delivered about 1,300 W for roughly 5 minutes. TheSolarLab says that above 1,200 W it lowers its voltage to keep running, and they found "no button for it, and no setting in the app to activate it." A 1,198 W load ran 38.5 minutes at 77% efficiency, and the unit cut off at about 6–7% remaining.
findings.source_title: OUPES Exodus 1200 Review: Good Deal or Complete Failure?
findings.note: Bench test by The Solar Lab. The page names no individual reviewer and shows no article date. This explains why the 1,500 W boost suits heaters but not loads that need full 120 V.

findings.value: 576 Wh; 700 W; 140 W USB-C; 4,000+ cycles to 80%; $399 (compare-at $819)
findings.note: Read from oupes.com store product data with storecheck.py. Exodus series, so the alternator charger exclusion above applies.

unsourced: I looked for a maker statement or manual page saying the Mega 1 Lite does or doesn't have a B2 expansion port. The direct product page and the B2 page returned HTTP 429 on oupes.com, and a web search found only the store listings, which make no expansion claim for the Lite.

I tried to open the Exodus 1200 user manual to confirm its port list and boost-mode wording. manuals.plus and device.report copies returned HTTP 403, and OUPES's own PDF wasn't reachable because oupes.com was rate-limiting.
I didn't measure or find a source for the Mega 1's UPS switchover time in milliseconds. The US listing says only "Seamless UPS Backup (2,000W Max)".
